## Investigación con agentes (Claude Opus 5.5; puede contener errores)
**Research notes: Is the U.S. blockade of Iranian seaborne crude still on? (2026‑10‑05, final)**

All three research agents have now reported back. These notes replace my two earlier versions; the first used invented figures and should be discarded entirely. [snippet] means the fact comes from a search-engine summary, not a page the agent read. Metaculus, Bloomberg, Vortexa and Kalshi pages could not be opened.

**1. What the resolution source says**
- **Metaculus "credible source" [snippet; the page returned an access error]:** "an online or print published article from a journalistic or academic source, information publicly posted by an authoritative source with specific knowledge or responsibility for the subject matter… provided in all cases that there is no significant controversy surrounding its correctness." It excludes unsourced blogs and social media. https://www.metaculus.com/faq/
- **Default rule:** if no credible report of a lifting or suspension exists by 23:59 UTC Oct 15, the question resolves YES.
- **Latest operational status:** the blockade is in force. No lifting or suspension has been reported since it was reinstated on Jul 14, 2026.
  - **Sep 30, CENTCOM (via APA, page read):** "CENTCOM forces have redirected 125 commercial vessels to ensure strict compliance." https://en.apa.az/america/us-says-125-vessels-diverted-in-iran-blockade-527432
  - **Oct 1, Bloomberg [snippet]:** "Iran Loaded No Oil Onto Tankers Last Month as US Blockade Bites." Kpler and Vortexa also show zero September loadings, down from about 210–250 kb/d in August. https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-01/iran-loaded-no-oil-onto-tankers-last-month-as-us-blockade-bites
  - **Oct 3, Fortune (page read):** exports are "virtually zero," per Kpler. About 90M barrels already at sea are expected to run out around mid‑October. https://fortune.com/2026/10/03/iran-currency-rial-dollar-record-low-blockade-oil-revenue-payments
    - Running out of barrels at sea is not a change in blockade status; the fine print says so.

**2. Timeline (everything before the question opened is background only)**
- **Feb 28, 2026:** the US–Israel war on Iran begins and Iran closes Hormuz.
- **Apr 13, 10:00 EDT:** the blockade begins. It applies to "vessels of all nations entering or departing Iranian ports." https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_naval_blockade_of_Iran
  - No executive order was found; the blockade rests on a presidential announcement plus CENTCOM statements.
- **Jun 17:** the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding is signed (one agent's source says Versailles instead). **Jun 18:** CENTCOM lifts the blockade. It had run about 66 days.
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamabad_Memorandum
  - https://www.npr.org/2026/06/18/nx-s1-5863517/trump-iran-deal-blockade-strait-hormuz [snippet]
- **Jul 7–8:** Iran attacks commercial ships and Trump says the memorandum is "over."
- **Jul 13:** Trump announces the blockade will return. **Jul 14:** it is reinstated. https://www.axios.com/2026/07/13/trump-iran-blockade-strait-hormuz ; https://www.cnn.com/2026/07/14/world/live-news/iran-war-trump
- **Jul 18:** Iran suspends its commitments under the memorandum.
- **Aug 17:** the memorandum's 60‑day window expires with no deal.
- **Enforcement since reinstatement:**
  - Aug 11: 55 vessels rerouted.
  - Sep 5: US forces disable the tankers Downy (off Kharg) and Stark 1. https://www.cnn.com/2026/09/05/middleeast/iran-us-tanker-kharg-intl
  - Sep 12: more than 100 vessels redirected.
  - Sep 30: 125 vessels redirected.

**3. Recent diplomacy (last ~2 weeks)**
- **~Sep 25–26:** Iran's foreign minister Araghchi proposes a 7‑day roadmap. The US would release about $12B in frozen funds, lift oil sanctions and end the blockade; Iran would then reopen Hormuz. https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/2026/9/26/trump-rejects-irans-seven-day-roadmap-to-reopen-strait-of-hormuz
- **Sep 26:** Trump calls it "not acceptable."
- **Sep 28:** Trump posts "I offered them NOTHING!" A US official says there will be "no deal unless nuclear issue addressed." https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-talks-strait-of-hormuz/
- **Sep 29:** Qatar mediates indirect talks in New York. The US wants one comprehensive deal centred on the nuclear issue. Al Jazeera reports Trump expects a deal after the **Nov 3 midterms**. https://aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/29/us-iran-talks-in-new-york-whats-the-latest
- **Sep 30:** Iran says it has received the official US response. Its contents have not been disclosed. https://english.aawsat.com/world/5324226-iran-says-received-us-response-its-proposal-end-war
- **Oct 3:** Camp David meeting on Iran. https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/trump-iran-war-us-midterm-elections-troops-deployment/
  - Trump says victory could come "right after the election."
  - The Theodore Roosevelt carrier group and the Makin Island amphibious group are heading to the region.
  - The G7 will release 100M barrels over 4 months.
- **Oct 4:** Ghalibaf, Iran's parliament speaker and chief negotiator, says Hormuz "will not open until our seven conditions… are met." https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/4/iran-says-strait-of-hormuz-to-remain-closed-until-us-meets-conditions
  - Iran is reportedly preparing a counter‑response [snippet].
  - Trump reportedly said Iran would be "choked out or bombed" [snippet].
- **Scheduled events Oct 5–15:** none confirmed. No US–Iran round, deadline or UN vote was found. Iran's counter‑response is pending with no date. The next anchor date is the Nov 3 midterms.
- **Oil price:** Brent was about $101.31 on Oct 5 [snippet, Trading Economics].

**4. Prediction markets (all seen Oct 5, ~06:15 UTC)**
- **Polymarket, "US announces end of Iranian blockade by…?"** https://polymarket.com/event/us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockade-byptptpt-20260713152715080

  | Deadline | Yes price | Volume |
  |---|---|---|
  | Oct 15 | 12¢ | $859K |
  | Oct 31 | 23¢ | $3.44M |
  | Dec 31 | 51.6¢ | $2.81M |

  - In early September, Oct 31 was at about 39% and Dec 31 at about 65% [snippet].
  - The event's total volume figure may be confused with another market (uncertain).
- **Polymarket, "Iran blockade lifted before Iran‑Oman Hormuz agreement?":** 26¢, $19.4K volume.
- **Manifold, "US x Iran permanent peace deal by Dec 31":** 22.9%, about 3.7K mana.
- **Kalshi:** current prices unavailable (the site rate-limited requests).

**5. Base rates**
- **Elapsed time:** about 83 days since Jul 14, about 149 days of blockade in total, and about 175 days since Apr 13. Ten days remain until resolution.

| Case | Duration | How it ended |
|---|---|---|
| Cuba quarantine, 1962 | ~4 weeks | Negotiated deal |
| Iran blockade, phase 1, 2026 | ~66 days | Memorandum with Iran; reversed 26 days later |
| Operation Earnest Will escorts, 1987–88 | ~14 months | Iran–Iraq ceasefire |
| Biafra | ~2.5 years | Military defeat |
| Beira Patrol (Rhodesia) | ~9.3 years | Made moot by Mozambique's independence |
| Iraq interception force | ~12.7 years | Regime change |
| Yemen, Gaza | Ongoing for years | Not formally ended |
| Venezuela tanker blockade, from Dec 2025 | Formally ongoing | Eased through licences, not a formal end |

- **Pattern:** blockades end through a deal, the end of a war, or regime change. Several have never formally ended, and a lift tied to a deal can be reversed.
- **Sources:** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beira_Patrol ; https://www.globalsecurity.org/military/ops/mio.htm ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%932026_United_States_oil_blockade_of_Venezuela

**Gaps**
- No Reuters or AP article was read directly.
- No TankerTrackers statement from September or October was found.
- The contents of the US response to Iran are unknown.
- Several sources mix up Iran's closure of Hormuz with the US blockade.

criterios: This question resolves YES if, as of 23:59 UTC on October 15, 2026, the United States is still enforcing a naval blockade (or equivalent naval interdiction regime) that is preventing routine seaborne crude oil exports from Iranian terminals, as described by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). It resolves NO if, on or before that time, the blockade has been formally lifted, suspended, or otherwise ended such that Iranian crude is again permitted to load and transit the Strait of Hormuz for export under normal commercial conditions. Reporting from a major wire service (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, AP) or tanker-tracking firms (Kpler, Vortexa, TankerTrackers.com) describing the operational status of the blockade will be used to resolve.
letra_pequena: Temporary transits of individual tankers under U.S. naval escort or special shuttle arrangements do not by themselves constitute an end to the blockade. The question concerns the formal/operational status of the U.S. interdiction regime, not the volume of any residual Iranian floating-storage barrels still being drawn down. If no credible source has reported a lifting or suspension of the blockade by the resolution time, the question resolves YES (reflecting continuation of the status quo).
razonamientos:
(a) **Time left:** About 10 days, until 23:59 UTC on October 15.

(b) **Status quo:** YES. The blockade is reportedly being enforced, and no lifting or suspension has been reported.

(c) **Reference class:** Wartime naval interdiction regimes generally last months or longer and usually end through a negotiated deal or a major change in the conflict. The historical sample is small, but it suggests a low chance of an established blockade ending in any particular 10-day period.

(d) **NO scenario:** The U.S. and Iran reach an agreement—or the U.S. unilaterally suspends enforcement—allowing routine Iranian crude exports to resume before the deadline.

(e) **YES scenario:** Talks remain unresolved and U.S. forces continue interdiction through October 15.

(f) **Resolution technicality:** A few tankers passing under special arrangements would not count as ending the blockade. Conversely, a credible report that it has been lifted or suspended would support NO even before export volumes recover.

Probability: 90%

(a) **Time left:** About ten days, until 23:59 UTC on October 15.

(b) **Status quo:** YES. The blockade is active, and no lifting or suspension has been reported.

(c) **Reference class:** Naval blockades and interdiction regimes generally last weeks to years and tend to end through a negotiated agreement or a wider change in the conflict. Given the small and varied sample, I would use a rough **5–15% base rate for ending within ten days**, not a precise historical frequency.

(d) **NO scenario:** The U.S. and Iran reach an unexpectedly quick agreement, and the U.S. lifts or suspends interdiction in time for Iranian crude to resume normal commercial export transit.

(e) **YES scenario:** Talks remain unresolved through October 15, and U.S. forces continue enforcing the blockade.

(f) **Resolution technicality:** A few escorted tankers or exports from floating storage would not make this a NO. The decisive issue is whether the interdiction regime has ended so crude can load and transit under normal commercial conditions. Absent a credible report of a lift or suspension by the deadline, the stated rule resolves YES.

The short horizon, stalled talks, and explicit status-quo resolution rule outweigh the possibility of a rapid deal.

Probability: 90%

**(a) Time left:** about 10 days, until 23:59 UTC on October 15, 2026.

**(b) Status quo:** the blockade is in force. CENTCOM reported 125 vessels redirected as of Sep 30, and Kpler and Vortexa show zero Iranian crude loadings in September. If nothing changes, this resolves YES.

**(c) Reference class and base rate:** naval blockades and interdiction regimes usually last months to years. They end through a negotiated deal, the end of a war, or regime change. The chance that any given 10-day window contains the lifting is low, roughly 5–10%. That is higher than usual here because Phase 1 ended suddenly with the June memorandum. Polymarket's ladder gives about 12% for an end announced by Oct 15 and 23% by Oct 31, on reasonable volume of about $0.86M. That is consistent with roughly a 1%-per-day hazard, and the market has been falling since early September.

**(d) NO scenario:** Iran's pending counter-response, or the Qatar-mediated track, produces a quick interim deal. Trump announces the blockade is suspended in exchange for Hormuz reopening, similar to the June 18 lift that followed the Islamabad memorandum. Wire services report it before Oct 15.

**(e) YES scenario:** the parties stay far apart. Trump rejected the 7-day roadmap, Ghalibaf insists on seven conditions, and the US says there is no deal without the nuclear issue being addressed. Trump signals a deal only "after the election" on Nov 3, and more carrier groups are deploying. The blockade simply continues through Oct 15.

**(f) Technicalities:**
- If nothing is reported, the question defaults to YES.
- Floating-storage barrels running out does not change the blockade's status.
- One-off escorted transits do not count as an end.
- A NO needs the blockade to be formally lifted or suspended so that Iranian crude can move normally.
- A preliminary announcement of a "deal in principle" with lifting scheduled after Oct 15 could be ambiguous. This slightly favors YES compared with the Polymarket "announces end" framing.

Overall, the probability of a formal lift within 10 days is about 8–10%.

Probability: 91%
